pool.text: Invasion of the empire by the Turks occurred after the Battle of Manzikert.
The first Ottoman attack on Athens involved a short-lived occupation under Ottoman generals.
Athens was captured by the Ottomans under the personal leadership of Sultan Mehmed II.
A lightning bolt struck the Propylaea, causing its destruction in the city.
The Acropolis was besieged by Venetians under Francesco Morosini during the Morean War.
The Venetians abandoned Athens again to the Ottomans on April 9.
A Greek insurgency captured the city before it fell back to the Ottomans.
The Ottoman forces remained in possession of Athens until their withdrawal in March.
The National Garden of Athens was completed as a green refuge.
The first line of the Athens Metro was constructed in the city.
The American-born Greek soprano Maria Callas settled in Athens for her teens.
The National Museum of Contemporary Art opened in a former brewery building.
Athens hosted the Summer Olympics, matching previous international multi-sport hosting duties.
The New Acropolis Museum opened and replaced the old museum on the Acropolis.
The Athens Stock Exchange was hit by the Greek government-debt crisis.
Athens joined the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities.
Athens was designated as the World Book Capital by UNESCO.
The National Art Gallery reopened after undergoing renovation work.
New metro stations connected the Port of Piraeus with Athens International Airport.
The Municipality inaugurated the Maria Callas Museum in a neoclassical building.
